title: TODO Application - React Frontend + Express Backend
problem_statement: Users need a simple, reliable way to capture, organize, and track daily tasks. Without a dedicated task management tool, tasks get lost in chat messages, sticky notes, or mental memory, leading to missed deadlines and reduced productivity. This application provides a focused TODO list interface where users can quickly add tasks, mark them as complete, and remove them — keeping the workflow as frictionless as possible.
target_users: Individual users managing personal daily tasks
Professionals tracking work items and action items
Students organizing assignments and study tasks
Anyone needing a lightweight, fast task tracking tool

functional_requirements.description: Users can view a list of all TODO items
acceptance_criteria: The application loads and displays all existing TODO items from the backend on page load
Each item shows its title text and completion status (checkbox or strikethrough)
An empty state message is shown when no tasks exist (e.g., 'No tasks yet. Add one above!')
The list updates automatically after any add/delete/toggle operation

functional_requirements.description: Users can add a new TODO item with a title
acceptance_criteria: An input field and 'Add' button are present above or inline with the task list
User can type a task title and submit via button click or Enter key press
The new task appears immediately in the list after successful creation
Empty or whitespace-only titles are rejected with a validation message
The input field is cleared after successful submission
A loading or disabled state is shown on the submit button while the request is in flight to prevent duplicate submissions

functional_requirements.description: Users can mark a TODO item as completed or uncompleted
acceptance_criteria: Each task has a checkbox or toggle that indicates its completion status
Clicking the toggle flips the task's completion state (completed ↔ uncompleted)
Completed tasks are visually distinguished (e.g., strikethrough text, grayed out, or moved to a separate section)
The state change persists after page refresh
Toggling completion on an already-completed task marks it as incomplete again

functional_requirements.description: Users can delete a TODO item
acceptance_criteria: Each task has a delete button or icon (e.g., trash can or '×')
Clicking delete removes the task from the list immediately
The deletion persists after page refresh
A confirmation step is shown before deletion to prevent accidental removal (e.g., confirm dialog or 'Are you sure?' prompt)

functional_requirements.description: Users can edit the title of an existing TODO item
acceptance_criteria: Users can click on a task title to enter inline edit mode
The title becomes an editable text field
Pressing Enter or clicking away saves the new title
Pressing Escape cancels the edit and restores the original title
Empty or whitespace-only edits are rejected

functional_requirements.description: Users can filter tasks by completion status
acceptance_criteria: Filter buttons/tabs allow viewing: All, Active (incomplete), and Completed tasks
The active filter is visually highlighted
Filtering is performed client-side for responsiveness
The filter state is preserved when tasks are added/removed/toggled

functional_requirements.description: The application handles API errors gracefully
acceptance_criteria: Network errors (timeout, server down) display a user-friendly error message
Failed operations (add/delete/toggle) show an error notification without crashing the app
The UI rolls back optimistic updates if the server request fails
A 'Retry' option is offered for failed operations where applicable

non_functional_requirements.description: Initial page load and task list fetch should complete within 1 second under normal network conditions
Task operations (add, toggle, delete) should feel instant via optimistic UI updates, with server sync completing within 500ms
non_functional_requirements.threshold: < 500ms server response time for CRUD operations

non_functional_requirements.description: The UI must be responsive and usable on mobile devices (320px width) through desktop (1920px+)
The application must be keyboard-accessible: all operations (add, toggle, delete, edit) should be achievable via keyboard alone
The interface should follow accessibility best practices (WCAG 2.1 Level AA minimum)
non_functional_requirements.threshold: WCAG 2.1 AA compliance — includes proper ARIA labels, focus management, color contrast ≥ 4.5:1

non_functional_requirements.description: Data must persist across application restarts and page refreshes
non_functional_requirements.threshold: Zero data loss on refresh or server restart (data stored durably in database/file)

non_functional_requirements.description: API endpoints must validate and sanitize all input to prevent injection attacks (XSS, NoSQL injection if using MongoDB)
non_functional_requirements.threshold: All inputs sanitized; Content-Security-Policy headers set

non_functional_requirements.description: If deployed, the API should enforce HTTPS and set secure HTTP headers
non_functional_requirements.threshold: HTTPS required; Helmet or equivalent middleware configured

non_functional_requirements.description: The application should handle up to 1000 tasks per user without noticeable UI degradation
non_functional_requirements.threshold: Smooth operation with 1000+ tasks (use of virtualized lists if needed)

constraints: Frontend must be built with React (JavaScript or TypeScript)
Backend must be built with Express.js (Node.js)
The frontend and backend communicate via a RESTful JSON API
The application must work in modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge — latest 2 versions)
No mandatory user authentication (single-user or anonymous usage assumed unless specified otherwise)
The solution should be runnable locally with minimal setup (e.g., npm install && npm start for each)
assumptions: The application is single-user or session-based; no multi-user support or authentication is required in the initial version
Task data is persisted in a local database (SQLite or JSON file) or in-memory store — not a cloud database
Each task has at minimum: a unique ID, a title string, a completion boolean, and a creation timestamp
The task title is plain text only (no Markdown, rich text, or attachments)
No real-time collaboration or WebSocket sync is needed
The application is not intended for production deployment as-is; it's a local development/learning project
Node.js and npm are pre-installed on the user's machine

clarifying_questions.question: Should the application support multiple users with authentication (login/signup), or is this a single-user application without login?
What should be used for data persistence — an in-memory store (data lost on server restart), a JSON file, SQLite, or a full database like PostgreSQL/MongoDB?
Beyond marking tasks as complete, should users be able to edit a task's title, add descriptions, set due dates, assign priorities, or organize tasks into categories/lists?
Should there be any filtering, sorting, or search capabilities (e.g., filter by 'completed', 'active', sort by date created)?
What is the deployment target — local-only development, cloud hosting (Vercel/Railway/Heroku), or containerized deployment?
Is TypeScript preferred over plain JavaScript for either the frontend or backend?
